# SK2241 — The regular expression pattern does not parse

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A compile-time-constant pattern is passed to a `System.Text.RegularExpressions` API that will reject it, so the call throws an `ArgumentException` the first time it runs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

`new Regex("(")` compiles, ships, and throws on the line that first executes it. The pattern is a constant, so whether it parses was decided when it was typed — nothing about the program's inputs can change the answer — and the only thing standing between the defect and the user is whether a test happened to reach that line. ⚠ **Finding it without running it is the entire value of the rule, and the measurement says nothing else does.** A probe built outside this repository, with empty `Directory.Build.props`/`.targets` above it, reports nothing at all on `new Regex("(")`, `new Regex("[a-")`, `new Regex("*abc")` and `Regex.IsMatch(s, "(")` — in the SDK's default state, and still nothing with `AnalysisMode=All`. ⚠ **The oracle is `Regex` itself, not a parser of this rule's own.** The analyzer constructs the pattern with the same options the call passes and reports what the constructor threw, so the rule cannot disagree with the runtime it is predicting. Parsing is not matching, so no pattern can make the analyzer backtrack.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
var matcher = new Regex("(unclosed");
```

Write:

```csharp
var matcher = new Regex(@"\(unclosed");
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **The `[GeneratedRegex]` half of the concept is already an on-by-default compiler error and is deliberately not reported.** `SYSLIB1042` — "The specified regex is invalid" — fails the build on `[GeneratedRegex("(")]` with no `AnalysisMode`, no `.editorconfig` and no analyzer package, which a probe confirmed behaviourally in the pristine default state. Reporting it here would be a second finding on a line that already does not compile. The rule registers on invocations and object creations only, so the attribute form is out of reach by construction. ⚠ **`SYSLIB1045` was probed and is orthogonal, not overlapping.** It is `Hidden` by default — it stays silent even at `AnalysisMode=All` and fires only when set explicitly — and when it does fire it fires *identically* on malformed and well-formed patterns, because it says "use `GeneratedRegexAttribute`" and never reads the pattern. ⚠ **Only a compile-time constant is examined.** A pattern built at runtime is a value this rule cannot have an opinion about, and an interpolated or concatenated pattern that Roslyn does not fold to a constant declines. ⚠ **The options argument has to be readable, because it decides what parses.** `RegexOptions.IgnorePatternWhitespace` and `RegexOptions.ECMAScript` change which patterns are legal, so a call passing options the model cannot fold to a constant declines rather than guessing — asking `Regex` the wrong question would produce exactly the false positive the bar forbids. ⚠ **"Suspicious" is not reported and the omission is deliberate.** A redundant or unusual construct is a judgement, and the half of that concept with an objective test — catastrophic backtracking — is already `SK5010`'s. What is left here is the half with no judgement in it at all: the pattern either parses or it does not, and `Regex` is the one that says which. There is no fix, because a pattern that does not parse does not say what it was meant to be. Generated code is excluded.
